status: DRAFT: written from general dental radiology criteria, needs dentist review
state_after_gate: An image is attached. It is a panoramic dental X-ray showing the teeth.

gate.q: Is this a dental X-ray showing teeth?
Does the image show both the upper and the lower row of teeth?
Is the image sharp enough to see individual teeth?
Is a large part of the image covered by text or an artefact?
Is the image a radiograph rather than a photograph, drawing or screenshot?
Is the jaw shown from ear to ear, as in a panoramic X-ray?
Is the contrast good enough to tell enamel from the darker inner tooth?
Is the image rotated or cut off so that part of one jaw is missing?
Is the image free of large bright objects covering the teeth, such as a bite block or jewellery?

features.q: Is there a dark area inside the crown of any tooth, the part above the gum?
Is there a dark area between two neighbouring teeth where they touch?
Is there a dark area beside or under a filling?
Does any dark area in a tooth reach towards the centre of the tooth?
Is any tooth heavily broken down, with most of its crown missing?
Does any tooth have a bright white filling?
Is any tooth missing from the row?
Is there an impacted tooth, lying sideways or buried in the bone?
Is there a dark area around the tip of a root?
Do all visible tooth crowns look evenly light, with no dark spots?
Is there a bright line inside a root, as from a root canal filling?
Is there a crown or cap on any tooth?
Is there visible loss of bone between the teeth?
Are the outer outlines of every tooth crown smooth and continuous?
Is there a dark spot on the biting surface of any back tooth?
Is there a dark notch at the neck of any tooth, near the gum line?
Is any tooth crown visibly darker than the crowns next to it?
Are the spaces between neighbouring teeth clear and uniform?
Is there a tooth with a large filling that covers most of its crown?
Is there a tooth with a visible gap between its crown and a filling?

discriminators.q: Is a dark area in a tooth crown clearly darker than the tooth around it and well defined?
Is a dark area on the chewing surface of a back tooth?
Is a dark area on the side of a tooth that touches its neighbour?
Does a dark area cross the outer white enamel layer of a tooth?
Could every dark area in the tooth row be explained by the normal gap between teeth or by a shadow?
Is there a dark area at the place where a filling meets the tooth?
Is the dark area inside the enamel or deeper?
Is the dark area triangular, pointing towards the centre of the tooth?
Is the dark area limited to a tooth that has no filling?
Is the darker area at the same place in both neighbouring teeth, as a shadow would be?
Is the darker area a straight band across several teeth?
Is there a clear sharp border between the dark area and the tooth around it?

deep.q: Does the dark area look different from the dark spaces between teeth?
Is the dark area in a tooth that has a normal-looking root?
Does the dark area extend from the outer surface inwards?
Is more than one tooth showing a dark area in its crown?
Is the outline of the crown broken or notched at the dark area?
Is the dark area bigger than a quarter of the crown width?
Does every dark spot sit on a tooth contact point or a chewing surface, where caries commonly starts?
Are all the tooth crowns evenly bright from edge to edge?
